why: Telemetry for the null-dereference case, derived from the two shares the incident text states. It is the corpus's first case whose evidence includes a log line that is a *checkpoint* rather than a decoration: the exception's frame is the only reading that names the failing line, and a metric cannot say 'a dereference' in words. The two shares are one fact seen from two sides -- the accounts the mapper wrote as null, and the requests that therefore failed -- so a corpus carrying either alone would let a reader mistake a population for a rate. Neither series moves at a magnitude a threshold would call large; what makes the case solvable is that they are the only two that move at all.

series.why: the checkpoint `cp-5xx-ratio` holds the share: a failure rate rather than an outage, and it belongs to one endpoint rather than to the service

series.quote: the field present but null rather than absent
series.why: the checkpoint `cp-null-share` holds the population: the accounts the mapper wrote as null after the migration, which is the set the guard admitted

logs.body: NullPointerException at com.storefront.reporting.SummaryMapper.summarize(): subscriptionState was present and null
logs.quote: Every stack trace ends in summarize() on the same line
logs.why: the checkpoint `cp-stack-trace` holds the frame: a reconstruction of the line the text describes, and the phrase it cites is the frame rather than a paraphrase of one

noTraces: the call throws inside the handler, and the text quotes the frame rather than a duration, so a span would carry a number the incident never gave.
